main_text.l: crinis modicè crispus præ teneritudine, & purpu-
rantem tempore malaciæ pontum retulit, & quan-
do vicinam terram leni allapsu circumfundit, fu-
rore fluctus & barbarie sedata. Genarum rubor
non supra modum, quod fœmineum, neq; rursum
carundem decorem offuscabat pallor. Nafus ela-
boratissimè detornatus, vt plurimum naturæ opi-
ficis artificium argueret. Oleum circumfusum So-
lisin modum fulgerabat, & splendore lucis palæ-
stram quasi radiisillustrabat. animo inde, Corin-
na, vulnerata maiorem accutioremque dolorem
sentio. Amatorios enim affectus commemorare
pudet fœminas,
Eth. GORGIAS ARISTIDI. XVI.
Cùm fœnore accepisti, gaudes; exactus dolcs.&
incidens in fœneratores metu percelleris, quasi fe-
ris quibusdam, incidere visus immanibus. & cir-
cum spectas triuia, & oculos coniicis ad porticus
evitare[?] cupiens fœneratores: ficuti nauigantes in
magna tempestate ad portum applicare defide-
rant. Sed & malum malo addis. Postquam enim
fœnori ab aliis acce peris,aliis reddis debitum,idem
aliquid faciens, quod ij qui se metu mortis præci-
pitant.Quoniam igitur fœnerati multiplex homi-
nibus est malum, & fabulosa ista hydra,cui sponte
renascebantur tot capita, multò est peius, caue ct-
jam[?] ne vel infomnis tibi fœneratione imagineris.
Sic enim libere adspicies solares[?] radios, & aërem in
terra leniter nimis & placide respirabis.
Rust. LOPHON PEDIADÆ. XVII.
Ne Leucippus. Milam[?] enim nobis agellus enu-
triuit

page.notes: Right margin: only cut-off fragments of marginal notes survive at the scan edge (about 16 short fragments, such as "tit", "bu", "fo", "m", "ig", "ns", "pi", "pe", "ef", "te", "al", "ci", "ni", "pl", "di"). They are too cropped to read; I have placed them approximately and marked each as illegible. Their exact positions beside the text are uncertain. The "Rust." before LOPHON is doubtful (the long s ligature makes it look like "Rust."). Possibly "Eust." is intended; read as printed. "dolcs" and "solares" are doubtful; "ct-jam" at the line break is doubtful. "Milam" is doubtful (the letters are faint). Running head and page number are at the top; the catchword and signature are absent.
